changes.motivation: The DB query row was being cast to the wrong branded type — `GitCommonPath` instead of `ProjectPath` — which would have caused type errors downstream when passing the value to APIs expecting `ProjectPath`.
changes.summary: Fixed `remove-worktree.ts` to brand `row.path` as `ProjectPath` (via the brand constructor) instead of incorrectly casting it as `GitCommonPath`. Also derived `GitCommonPath` via `git.commonDir(projectPath)` for use with `worktreeList` and `deleteBranch`.

changes.motivation: Kysely table interfaces used plain `string` for all columns, requiring manual branding at every query call site and making incorrect casts easy to write.
changes.summary: Updated `Store/types.ts` Kysely table interfaces (`MuxProjectsTable`, `MuxWorktreesTable`) to use branded types (`ProjectId`, `ProjectPath`, `BranchName`, `WorktreeId`) instead of raw `string`. Kysely propagates these through all query result types automatically.

changes.motivation: After the Store types were updated to return branded types directly, the manual `BranchName(...)` and `ProjectPath(...)` calls in `remove-worktree.ts` became redundant.
changes.summary: Removed manual branding calls in `remove-worktree.ts`; `row.branch` and `row.path` are now correctly typed by Kysely without any explicit cast or brand constructor.

problems: Initial fix applied the wrong branded type (`GitCommonPath` instead of `ProjectPath`) to `row.path`. The column stores a project path, not a git common dir — the difference is subtle but semantically important, and the existing column name `path` with no inline comment about what kind of path it stores made the mistake easy. A doc comment on the `MuxProjectsTable.path` field clarifying it is a `ProjectPath` (i.e. the working-tree root, distinct from the git common dir) would prevent this.

After removing the destructured `branch` variable, the agent failed to update references to `branch` on lines 39 and 47, leaving broken identifiers. This required a follow-up edit. The root cause was editing in two steps (removing the destructuring first, then the usage sites) without reading the full resulting file between edits.
